findings.message: Choice 'turn-mirror' (story.r1.json lines 140-146) can never be locked. Its requirement (soft-cloth + damp-mirror) is identical to 'wipe-mirror' on 'threshold' (lines 120-126), which is the only way into 'climax', and no passage uses removeItems or any effect that removes an item or clue. Every player who reaches 'climax' already holds both, so the lock and its lockedHint are dead. As a result ending-beam vs ending-help is a free choice, not a reward for finding the cloth and clue. Fix: remove the redundant requirement, or give 'climax' a genuinely different gate (for example a second clue or item found in the story).

Mixed message with the theme 'asking for help'. ending-help (lines 162-172) is framed as the lesser result ('It took much longer', boats come home late, kind bittersweet). The text in bench-clue and ending-help says asking for help is right and brave. Consider making the help ending clearly good, or making the beam ending depend on a different skill.

A player who climbs without the cloth or the clue has no way back from 'threshold' (lines 119-128). The only open choice is 'run-with-lantern', which leads to the setback ending. The lockedHint ('You need a soft cloth and a clue about the mirror.', line 125) does not say where to look, and the player cannot go back to look. Add a 'go back down' choice to gathering, or make the hint point to the shed and to Gran Tull.

Logic gap. The premise says the lamp 'went dark', but the clue ('damp-mirror') explains a dim lamp. The wick is cold and unlit in 'threshold' (line 116). In 'climax' (line 135) Fen lights the wick with no match, taper or other item. A short line saying who left the lamp unlit, or where the light comes from, would close this. Gran Tull is a retired keeper who sits on a bench while the boats are lost. That is a mild plausibility issue.

Item use is inconsistent. The label for 'turn-mirror' says 'Turn the mirror with the cloth' (line 142) but the cloth is for wiping. The hint says the cloth and clue let Fen 'turn it well' (line 145), which nothing in the story supports.

The 'small lantern' in 'run-with-lantern' (line 127) and ending-lantern is not an item or earlier object. It appears from nowhere. In the same passage Gran Tull is suddenly on the dock, although she was last on the bench. Both are small continuity slips.

Routes traced in the JSON. (1) ending-lantern: start -> to-shed or to-bench -> ... -> gathering -> gather-climb -> threshold -> run-with-lantern, which is open with no items. (2) ending-help: start -> to-shed -> open-chest (soft-cloth) -> chest-to-tower -> gather-bench -> ask-more (damp-mirror) -> clue-to-tower -> gather-climb -> wipe-mirror -> climax -> call-gran. (3) ending-beam: the same prefix, then turn-mirror. The mirror route needs both the shed and the bench, and the gathering hub allows this. All 11 passages are reachable, there are no dead ends, and the three endings match the brief's endingTarget of 3. Item and clue ids (soft-cloth, damp-mirror) are defined and used consistently.

Word sets carry their declared pattern. sh: ship, shell, fish, shed, shut all have initial or final sh and are closed syllables. ch: chest, chain, bench, much all have the /ch/ digraph. th: path, thick, moth, cloth all have voiceless th. Minimums are met: sh 18/10, ch 15/8, th 19/8. Every word is used at least twice, and each set appears on the shortest route to all three endings.

'chain' carries the ch digraph but is a vowel-team syllable (ai), not a closed syllable. It will not support closed-syllable practice, and a reader still learning vowel teams may find it harder than chest/bench/much. It appears only twice (shed: 'Fen lifted the chain and pushed'; ending-help: 'the chain that turns the mirror'), so the weave plan's four-plus placements (opening, path-a, threshold, climax) were not realised. Consider swapping it for a closed-syllable ch word such as 'chop' or 'chip', or adding exposures.

Low exposure for some words: chain 2, shut 2, moth 2. For a new reader, two exposures is thin. The weave comparison reports ok because only set totals are checked: ch actual 15 vs planned 18. Per-word repetition is not checked.

The 'per ending route' counts overstate what a child reads. The analyzer counts passage titles and every choice label, including options on branches not taken and locked choices. Example: on the shortest route to ending-lantern (start, bench, bench-clue, gathering, threshold), 'chest' appears only in the gathering label 'Go back to the shed and the chest'. 'chain' never appears there. 'Bench' is counted once from the title 'Gran Tull on the Bench'. The ch set still appears on every route (bench, much), but with fewer exposures than the 8 reported for ending-lantern.

Natural-weave check: most uses read naturally ('Out at sea, every ship and fishing boat needed that light', 'Gran Tull sat on the bench in a thick wool coat', 'The shed door was shut'). A few look placed to hit the plan. 'A moth tapped on the window. Pip chased it down the path.' is tacked onto the clue passage and does nothing for the plot. 'Gran Tull ... gave Fen a shell from her coat' is unmotivated. 'A wipe will fix it, and much faster than you think' is slightly stiff. Narrative designer may wish to smooth these; I am not rewriting passages.

False positive for parents (digraph-th, 149 matches): most of this count is the high-frequency voiced-th words the, that, than, their, then, there, they, thing, think, with. These are real th spellings but a different sound from the voiceless th in path/thick/moth/cloth. 'lighthouse' is a false positive: the t and h belong to separate syllables (light-house) and are not a digraph. 'thought' ('Fen thought about the path', gathering) matches th but is an irregular -ough word and is not decodable at this stage.

False positives for parents (closed-syllable, 366 matches): the detector accepts any word with one vowel letter and 6 letters or fewer ending in a consonant. That wrongly includes 'bright', 'might', 'night' (igh vowel team); 'call', 'small', 'wall', 'all' (a before ll sounds /aw/); and 'far', 'dark', 'for', 'her', 'first' (r-controlled). It also includes 'old', 'told', 'kind', 'wild' (long vowel by pattern) and 'what', 'was' (irregular). True short-vowel closed syllables in the text include ship, shed, shut, chest, bench, much, path, thick, moth, cloth, fish, shell, dim, wick, tap, and, kept, hung, step, dock, glass and brass.

Other detector notes: 'shelf', 'shines', 'shone', 'dish', 'fresh', 'pushed' and 'shouts' are real sh digraphs and are not false positives. 'sure' is the reverse case: it says /sh/ but has no sh spelling, so the detector misses it, and it is irregular. 'whole' (digraph-wh, untargeted) is a false positive: it is pronounced /h/. 'pushed' and 'chased' read as -ed suffix words (/t/ sounds). 'shell', 'small', 'smell', 'tell', 'brass' and 'glass' are FLOSS, which is fine.

Vocabulary load for an early reader on sh/ch/th and closed syllables. Multisyllable or irregular words that are not decodable at this stage: lighthouse, harbour (British -our), lantern, mirror, tower, window, pocket, fluttered, folded, across, afraid, again, every, answer, thought, know/knew, meant, many, years, coat, wool, brave, wipe, flame, gave, came, home, shone (silent-e), and stairs, air, beam, boat (vowel teams). The glossary covers only lighthouse, lantern, harbour, mirror. Words such as tower, window, answer, thought and across are not covered. Highest-frequency sight words (the, was, said, you, to, of, one, they, her, she, could, would, were, do) are expected. New continuity contradiction caused by the match-tin fix. In bench-clue (story.r3.json line 90) Gran Tull says 'My knees are too old for those stairs.' But ending-beam (line 153) says 'Gran Tull came up the stairs and gave Fen a hug', and ending-help (line 162) says 'Gran Tull climbed up, slow but sure, and put a hand on the chain.' Both triumph endings undo the reason she gave for not climbing. Fix: change ending-beam so Gran Tull meets Fen at the foot of the tower or on the path. Change ending-help so Fen goes down to get her, or so she gives the reason a different way (for example, she climbs 'one slow step at a time' after saying it would be worth it), or drop the knees line in bench-clue and give another reason for the match tin.

In ending-help (lines 162-165) the call-gran choice says Fen 'called down the stairs', but Gran Tull was last seen on the bench outside. She can hear a call from the lamp room only if she is at the tower door. Related to the major finding. Say that she waits at the foot of the tower, or that Pip fetches her.

Dark versus dim. The premise and start (line 61) say the lamp is dark. The clue (damp-mirror, line 36, and bench-clue line 89) explains a dim lamp. In threshold (line 117) the wick is simply cold and unlit, so the mirror is not what made it 'go dark'. The story still works, because Fen cleans the mirror and lights the wick. One line in threshold or bench-clue that says the wick went out in the wind and the mirror made it worse would close this cleanly.

The ending id 'ending-lantern' (line 177) and the 'run-to-dock' choice are left over from the removed lantern. This is cosmetic and affects only authors and reports. The setback ending itself is consistent: Fen runs to the dock, there is no lantern, and Gran Tull walks down the path to meet Fen.

The key clue uses four different words for one idea, and one is ambiguous. bench says "Look at the glass, not the flame". bench-clue then says "It leaves a film on the brass mirror", then "the misty mirror made the light dim".
